messages:
jess (support): heads-up, Acme on chat — they see p99 spikes since ~09:00 UTC. They pasted our dashboard and support's quickview and numbers don't match. they're escalated. can someone triage? :grimacing:

maria: on it. which dashboard are they looking at? the per-route p99 or the global agg?

jess (support): they sent screenshots: the customer view (support console) shows p99 ~1.8s, our public eng dashboard shows ~400ms. they say errors/latency started after midnight deploy.

liam: pinging metrics-bot for raw query and histograms for the last 2h for route=/v1/generate for acme-org.

metrics-bot: Query run: 
```
SELECT
  toStartOfMinute(timestamp) as minute,
  uniqExact(request_id) as requests,
  quantile(0.99)(latency_ms) as p99_ms
FROM http_requests
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND org_id = 'acme-org' AND timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 2 HOUR
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute
```
Result: p99 peaked at 1800ms at 09:07 UTC, baseline ~380ms.

dan: wait— that query is on the raw events table. our eng dashboard uses the zero-agg rollups (5m rollup table) which stores TDigest summaries and uses `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...)) )` over those histograms. two likely causes: 1) rollup ingestion lag/double-aggregation bug, 2) difference in quantile algorithm (exact vs TDigest approx).

liam: digging: we have a recent change in the rollup ingestion that switched from TDigest compression 100 -> 256 to improve memory; that can change tails. also the rollup pipeline now batches events per shard differently after the midnight deploy.

maria: can we reproduce by comparing per-minute exact quantile vs reconstructing quantile from histograms? run both for same minute slice.

metrics-bot: Running side-by-side sample for 09:06-09:08 UTC...

metrics-bot: Exact quantile query (raw events) returned 420ms (p50), 800ms (p95), 1800ms (p99).

metrics-bot: Histogram-based quantile (rollups) using histogram_quantile gave 420ms (p50), 760ms (p95), 420ms (p99). <-- big discrepancy at p99.

dan: ah — histogram_quantile on our rolled histograms is returning p99 ~= p50. that's a red flag. Could be bucket boundaries getting misapplied or rollup histogram reset. Did the deploy change histogram bucket scheme?

liam: I checked the rollup job: we accidentally started emitting histograms with 'linear' buckets for one shard group due to a config fallback. other shards still emit exponential buckets. When Prometheus-style histogram_quantile aggregates mismatched bucket sets, results are wrong.

maria: nice find. so the dashboard that reads rollups aggregates histograms across shards and ends up mixing bucket schemas — that would collapse the tail. support view uses raw events so it shows the real p99.

jess (support): can we tell Acme what happened? they want a mitigation now.

dan: immediate mitigation: 1) set dashboard to query raw events for p99 until rollups fixed (cheap for 2h sampling window), 2) roll back the rollup config change for the affected shard group, 3) add an alert if histogram bucket schema mismatch is detected.

liam: I can patch the rollup job to force bucket schema to 'exponential_v2' and trigger a small reprocess for the last 30m rollups. rolling back config now.

ops-bot: Deploy job queued: rollup-config-rollback -> shard-group-12. ETA ~4m.

maria: also adding a temporary note to the SRE dashboard header: "p99 values may be incorrect during 08:45-09:30 UTC due to rollup bucket mismatch; use raw-events panel for exact tail."

metrics-bot: after rollback, re-run comparison for 09:06-09:08 UTC. histogram_quantile now returns p99 ~1780ms, matching raw events.

dan: great. postmortem items: change validation in rollup ingestion to validate bucket schemas, add unit test for histogram merges, and make support dashboard fallback to raw-events for tail calc when compression/format changes detected.

jess (support): i'll update Acme: was a rollup bucket schema mismatch from recent deploy, fixed and reprocessed. apology and offered 1 week of premium support credit. they asked for the timeline — can we provide?

liam: timeline: 00:02 UTC midnight deploy introduced config fallback; anomaly surfaced at ~08:45; Acme escalated at 09:00; rollback at 09:12; reprocess completed at 09:18; verified at 09:20.

maria: creating incident ticket and tagging Product + Observability. will add the mitigation and follow-ups.

jess (support): thanks everyone. please @me in the ticket when done; i'll close the loop with the customer. :thumbsup:
